summary: Follow Builders 今日捕捉到 28 条 X 动态、1 集播客、0 篇博客；本站精选 9 条高信号内容。

featured.title: Guillermo Rauch · Vercel CEO
featured.summaryEn: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch wrote a long post-mortem on an agent sandbox security challenge. He splits agent escapes into two classes: (1) "escape the network" — the OpenAI incident, where an agent without internet access gained it by hacking another system; and (2) "escape the matrix" — breaking the virtualization boundary itself. In this challenge, a white-hat researcher armed with a swarm of AI agents pierced the Linux virtualization boundary that nearly every cloud sandbox provider relies on. Vercel moved quick…
featured.insightZh: Vercel CEO Guillermo Rauch 发长文复盘了一次 Agent 沙箱安全挑战。他把 Agent 逃逸分成两类：①「逃出网络」——OpenAI 那次事件就是这一类，一个本不该联网的 Agent 通过攻击另一个系统拿到了网络访问；②「逃出矩阵」——直接打穿虚拟化边界。这次挑战里，一位白帽研究员带着一群 AI Agent，凭专业能力和耐心「刺穿」了几乎所有云沙箱厂商都依赖的 Linux 虚拟化边界。Vercel 收到报告后快速修补，没有发现客户数据泄露的证据，并和多家行业伙伴一起做了更大范围的防护。他的结论是：Agent containment 会成为每家 AI 基础设施公司最重要的优先事项之一。另外他预告明天回到「一切开始的地方」办活动。

featured.title: Thariq · Anthropic Claude Code
featured.summaryEn: Thariq from Anthropic's Claude Code team refined his old advice to "be technical," saying it isn't precise enough. If you're technical, you need to be in the details of the right parts of the code; if you're non-technical, being in the details means knowing how things work at the right level. He also shared a piece titled "Today's Weather: Partly Agentic."
featured.insightZh: Claude Code 团队的 Thariq 修正了自己以前常说的「要懂技术」：这个说法不够准确。技术背景的人需要深入到代码里正确的那部分细节；非技术背景的人，「深入细节」意味着在合适的抽象层次上理解系统如何运作。另外他还分享了一篇标题为「今日天气：局部 Agentic」的内容。

featured.title: How Hugging Face's Investor Spots Winners
featured.summaryEn: As AI makes coding faster, the most valuable skill becomes turning user behavior into product insight and iterating rapidly; at the earliest stage, back technical founders whose "pivot foot" is the technology rather than a vertical market. Dan Shipper opened with model reviews: Google launched Gemini Argon 4 and Meta launched a new frontier model (named Wonder/Muse in the transcript). Every's hands-on testing suggests Muse is benchmark-maxed — about 50% on his senior engineer task and a middling writer — while Gemini 4 is weak at coding (~20%) but is now his favorite writing model, beating Astra and Claude and roughly doubling his productivity. He also previewed his 8,000-word piece "How Codex Happened." In the main interview, Natalia Quintero talks with Matt Hartman of Factorial Capital, who helped make the first investment in Hugging Face at Betaworks (described as acquired by NVIDIA…
featured.insightZh: AI 让写代码变快之后，最值钱的能力是「从用户行为中提炼产品洞察并快速迭代」；早期投资更应押注技术型创始人，因为他们的「轴心脚」是技术而不是某个垂直市场。 开场 Dan Shipper 先做了本周模型点评：Google 发布 Gemini Argon 4、Meta 也发布了新前沿模型（转录中名称为 Wonder/Muse）。Every 的实测认为 Muse 有「刷榜」嫌疑，在其高级工程师基准任务上只拿到约 50%，写作也中规中矩；Gemini 4 编码一般（约 20%），但被他评为目前最喜欢的写作模型，超过 Astra 和 Claude，帮他把写作效率提升约两倍。他还预告了长文《How Codex Happened》。 正片由 Every AI 咨询负责人 Natalia Quintero 访谈 Factorial Capital 创始管理合伙人 Matt Hartman。他在 Betaworks 时参与了 Hugging Face 的第一笔投资（节目中称其上月被 NVIDIA 以 130 亿美元收购）。Hugging Face 最初是给青少年的聊天机器人，团队诚实面对糟糕的留存，把 Transformers 移植到 PyTorch 开源后走红，最终转型为开源 AI 社区。他总结的关键决策：坦诚看待留存、开源 Transformers、把权重托管从 GitHub 迁到自己的 Hub、以及坚持开源不变而对模型类型保持灵活。 Hartman 的投资方法是寻找「新近在技术上成为可能」或「新近可编程」的东西，并假设早期公司一定会转型——技术型团队可以带着同一种数据形态的洞察跨行业转型，而行业高管型团队往往被锁在原垂直领域。Factorial 是单一 GP 加 12 位风险合伙人的结构（包括 Hugging Face CEO Clem、Venmo 联创等），被投公司不断推荐新的技术创始人，形成「家族树」式网络。他认为「赢得的洞察」（世界上只有少数人有机会学到的东西）是重要信号；迭代周期从两个月压缩到两天，使理解用户并转化为产品的人价值指数级上升，分发也比以往更重要。

items.title: Aditya Agarwal · South Park Commons 普通合伙人、前 Dropbox CTO
items.summaryEn: Aditya Agarwal announced a new South Park Commons experiment: $200K, uncapped, for a handful of "unapologetically maximalist thinkers" pursuing truly out-there ideas. The tension he describes: technological progress has never been this rapid, yet capital keeps flowing to consensus teams, markets, and terms. He wants to rewrite the capital stack — a nuclear company shouldn't raise the same seed round as an AI app. The $200K is no-downside fuel to explore a hard problem, after which SPC helps shape the right downstr…
items.insightZh: Aditya Agarwal 宣布 South Park Commons 的新实验：给少数「毫不掩饰的极致主义者」每人 20 万美元、无估值上限，去尝试真正离谱的想法。他的逻辑是两个矛盾并存：技术进步前所未有地快，似乎没有什么不可能；但资本却在流向共识团队、共识市场、共识条款。他认为应该重写资本结构——做核能的公司不该和 AI 应用拿一样的种子轮。这笔钱被定位为探索难题的「无下行燃料」，之后 SPC 再帮团队找到合适形态的后续资本。

items.title: Garry Tan · Y Combinator 总裁兼 CEO
items.summaryEn: Garry Tan kept pushing back on California's Prop 40, which he calls an "asset seizure tax." His example: a founder owning 50% of a $10B company owes 5% — $500M — on $1B of illiquid paper wealth, which no one will lend against; in this case it's effectively a 50% tax, not 5%. He argues the academics behind it don't understand how startups and innovation happen and that the policy will kill the golden goose.
items.insightZh: Garry Tan 继续反对加州 40 号提案（他称之为「资产没收税」）。他举例：一个持股 50%、公司估值 100 亿美元的创始人，按 5% 税率要交 5 亿美元，相当于其 10 亿美元纸面财富的一半，而这些资产完全不流动、根本借不到钱——在这个简单例子里实际是 50% 的税而非 5%。他批评支持方的学者不理解创业公司和创新如何发生，政策会「杀死下金蛋的鹅」。

items.title: Nikunj Kothari · FPV Ventures 合伙人
items.summaryEn: Nikunj Kothari argues venture is deceptively simple: (1) win the right to (2) find and invest in exceptional founders (3) just before it's consensus (4) consistently every year. Most VCs get one right; greatness requires all four, and consistency is the hardest and least discussed — Djokovic-style, enjoying hitting the ball every day and focusing on the next point. He also joked that Astra at 7pm, like a toddler at 7pm, isn't following instructions well.
items.insightZh: Nikunj Kothari 总结了风险投资看似简单的四件事：①赢得投资资格；②找到并投资卓越创始人；③在它变成「共识」之前出手；④每年持续做到。大多数 VC 只能做对其中一项，真正伟大的必须全部做对，而「持续正确」最难也最少被讨论——要像德约科维奇那样每天享受击球、只关注下一分。他还吐槽晚上 7 点的 Astra 和蹒跚学步的孩子一样「不太听指令」。

items.title: Dan Shipper · Every CEO
items.summaryEn: Every CEO Dan Shipper flagged a "must read," and shared what he calls the future of communications at work — "if you're still sending a deck, ngmi." He also noted there are "wonders to behold" in Every's Slack right now.
items.insightZh: Every CEO Dan Shipper 推荐了一篇「必读」文章，并断言他分享的内容代表了职场沟通的未来——「如果你还在发 PPT，就要被淘汰了」。他还提到 Every 的 Slack 里此刻「有很多奇妙的东西」。

items.title: Peter Yang · 产品负责人、AI 教程创作者
items.summaryEn: Peter Yang found out his 8-year-old used ChatGPT to answer her math homework — instead of being mad, he was quite impressed.
items.insightZh: Peter Yang 发现 8 岁的女儿用 ChatGPT 解出了数学作业，他没有生气，反而相当佩服。

items.title: Zara Zhang · Builder、Follow Builders 作者
items.summaryEn: Zara Zhang built a playful wishlist website, suggesting your next wedding, baby, or birthday gift registry could look like this, and shared a playable link plus the design inspiration.
items.insightZh: Zara Zhang 做了一个好玩的心愿单网站，并建议下一次婚礼、宝宝或生日礼物清单都可以做成这种形式，同时附上了可体验链接和设计灵感来源。
